description: Early traction alopecia is often reversible. Advanced traction alopecia is manageable. Here's how trichoscopy at 200x tells the difference, honestly.
subtitle: Early traction often recovers. Here is how we tell where your hairline sits today.

note.text: Traction alopecia is one of the conditions I care about most, because so many women feel guilt about the styles they loved. Please let that go. What matters now is how much life is left in those follicles, and caught early, that is often a lot. Gentler habits and consistent care can make a real difference.

shortAnswer.text: Early traction alopecia is often reversible, while advanced traction alopecia with follicular scarring may not fully regrow. A 200x scalp read helps separate the stages by showing whether follicular openings and miniaturized hairs remain. The result can vary across one hairline, so styling history, tenderness, bumps, and each section's magnified appearance guide realistic expectations.
takeaways: Use the scalp read to narrow the question.

body.toc: Sometimes Yes, Sometimes Partly, And The Read Tell
body.text: Sometimes Yes, Sometimes Partly, And The Read Tells You Which
If you have been asking whether it is too late for your edges, you deserve a real answer from someone who can actually see what is left.

body.toc: If You Have Said Any Of These, Read The Next Part
body.text: If You Have Said Any Of These, Read The Next Part

Long-standing tension can replace the follicle with fibrous tissue. When that happens, the follicular opening closes and the surface smooths over. Scarred follicles do not regrow. There is no product, injection or protocol that brings back a follicle that is no longer there, and anyone who tells you otherwise is selling you a year you cannot get back.
What Follicular Scarring Means

Manageable care still exists at that stage. The border beside a scarred band usually still holds viable follicles, and protecting those is the difference between a line that holds and a line that keeps moving. Full regrowth of the scarred band may not happen, and we will tell you that on the first visit rather than the sixth.

body.toc: What We Look For At 200x, Stage By Stage
body.text: What We Look For At 200x, Stage By Stage

A hairline can hold more than one stage at once. One section may still show follicular openings and small hairs, while another looks smoother. We examine the margin section by section rather than forcing the whole area into one label.

body.toc: The $99 Discovery Tells You If It's Reversible
body.text: The $99 Discovery Tells You If It's Reversible

The Discovery is designed to replace a mirror-based guess with a magnified baseline. You watch as we move along the affected area, document what remains, and explain which sections may still have recovery potential and which may need a management goal.

body.toc: What The Work Looks Like At Each Stage
body.text: What The Work Looks Like At Each Stage

Early and advanced areas require different work. Where follicles remain, reducing tension and supporting recovery are central. Where scarring has closed the openings, the honest goal changes, and we will not sell regrowth where the scalp does not support that promise.

body.text: The purpose of staging is not to frighten you. It is to stop wasting time on a plan designed for a different condition or a different point in the process.
What your styling history adds

We ask where tension has been concentrated, how long the style was worn, whether the same areas were repeatedly stressed, and when tenderness or bumps appeared. That history helps the magnified picture make sense without turning the appointment into a lecture about how you wear your hair.

Reversible and manageable are different outcomes, and both deserve a clear plan. Results not typical. Individual results will vary.
body.title: We will tell you what the scalp supports.

body.text: If openings and miniaturized hairs remain, there may be meaningful work to do. If scarring has closed an area, knowing that now protects you from spending more time and money on claims the scalp cannot support.
Clarity is not giving up. It is the point where care becomes more precise, expectations become kinder, and the next decision finally fits the stage you are in.

faq.a: Early traction alopecia is often reversible when follicles remain present and the pulling load is removed. Advanced areas with scarring may not fully regrow. Results not typical. Individual results will vary.

faq.q: How can you tell whether follicles remain?
faq.a: A 200x scalp read can show whether follicular openings and miniaturized hairs remain along the affected margin. A smooth appearance in the mirror is not enough to stage every section accurately.

faq.q: Can one hairline have more than one stage?
faq.a: Yes. One section may still show openings and small hairs while another appears closed or scarred. That mixed picture is why expectations and care may differ from one area to the next.

faq.q: What should I bring to a traction alopecia evaluation?
faq.a: Bring the styling timeline, where tension was repeatedly concentrated, when tenderness or bumps appeared, how the area has changed, and what you have already tried. That context helps the magnified picture make sense.
